Patient is ___ yo female with a past medical history of HTN, HLD,

Given her cognitive impairment and poor short term memory, it is 
difficult to assess whether acute changes have recently occured 
in the setting of the findings on imaging.

Her mental status is 
notable for a MOCA score of 16 on ___, with most prominent 
deficits in executive functioning, attention, and memory.

The 
reported and documented history of slowly progressive worsening 
cognitive decline in the setting of poor memory and some 
impairments in executive function, with preserved social graces, 
is consistent with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease, although 
the subtle hyperintensities seen in both cerebral hemispheres on

MRI are suggestive of previous infarcts, raising the possibility 
of vascular dementia, or AD complicated by vascular dementia.

Moreover, her exam is notable for dysdiadochokinesia, more 
pronounced on the R side, correlating with MRI suggestive of 
acute infarct in the R cerebellar hemisphere.

Given the 
cerebellar location, Ms. ___ stroke was likely embolic.
Stroke workup: A1C 6.3, likely prediabetic; FLP with LDL 40, HDL
68, at goal.

Vascular imaging also revealed that Ms. ___ had a right 
carotid artery 80% blockage.

As she is not likely to be a good 
surgical candidate for this, and as also this was not a source 
of her stroke, we did not pursue a surgical evaluation.

For Ms. ___ cerebellar stroke, pt was placed on aspirin 325 
mg daily.

As pt's SBP was elevated (in the high 150s) during this 
admission, we continued her home atenolol, and increased dose of 
enalapril to 20 mg BID

Should she require further BP control, consider switching 
atenolol to carvedilol, given nonselective effects of carvedilol 
on alpha 1 receptors.
